en: The dyad of "dissociated from the taints and accompanied by taints" and the triad of "wholesome."

Dependent on a wholesome state dissociated from the taints (āsava) but subject to the taints, there arises a state dissociated from the taints, not free from the taints, and unwholesome, by way of root condition … one.

Dependent on a wholesome state dissociated from the taints and free from the taints, there arises a state dissociated from the taints, not free from the taints, and unwholesome, by way of root condition … one. Under root [condition] there are two … pe … under non-disappearance there are two.

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the taints (*āsava*), subject to the taints (*sāsava*), and unwholesome (*akusala*), there arises a state that is dissociated from the taints, not subject to the taints, and not unwholesome, by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*). [Under] root [condition], one; ... pe ... [under] non-disappearance condition, one.

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the taints, subject to the taints, and indeterminate (*abyākata*), there arises a state that is dissociated from the taints, not subject to the taints, and not indeterminate, by way of root-condition. Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the taints, subject to the taints, and indeterminate...

A state that is dissociated from the taints (āsava), is neither a taint itself nor indeterminate (abyākata), arises by way of the root-condition (hetu-paccaya) … [In the case of] roots, there are two; … [and so on] … in the case of non-disappearance (avigata), there are two.
The Chapter on Taints is finished.
